findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the ordering value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. The audit-log endpoint that uses this paginator orders by -datetime, so the ordering value is a datetime: build_cursor will raise TypeError when a non-empty page is returned, and any cursor round-trip compares a datetime column against a millisecond integer rather than a datetime. The optimized audit-log path therefore returns 500 or incorrect results instead of functioning as a faster DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Unrelated audit-log endpoint exposes an unvetted negative-offset pagination path
findings.body: This spans-buffer change also adds a new optimized_pagination mode to the control-silo audit-log API. It is enabled for organization members with has_global_access, not only superusers, while pagination cursors and their offsets are client-controlled. Combined with OptimizedCursorPaginator's explicit negative-offset handling, this exposes an untested privileged pagination mode whose stated boundary handling is not provided by the underlying ORM; the unrelated API surface should not ship as part of the spans-buffer optimization.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing does not work on Django querysets
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, this code slices the queryset as queryset[negative:stop]. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError; they do not automatically handle or wrap negative slices as the comment claims. A crafted or generated prev/negative cursor therefore causes a 500 instead of advanced pagination. BasePaginator's changed logic at line 182 likewise leaves negative offsets untouched for is_prev cursors.

findings.title: Set-to-sorted-set conversion has no migration for in-flight Redis segments
findings.body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created before deployment are Redis sets, but process_spans now issues ZADD against them, add-buffer.lua issues ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE against them, and _load_segment_data issues ZSCAN against them. Those commands return WRONGTYPE for pre-existing segments, so batches and flushes can fail until the old keys expire, and a rollback would similarly break newly created sorted sets. The change needs a key-version bump, drain, or explicit type migration.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE corrupts scores for spans present in both merged sets
findings.body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls omit an AGGREGATE argument, so Redis defaults to SUM. When the same payload/member exists in the destination and source sets, for example after redelivery or an earlier partial merge, its end_timestamp_precise score is doubled. That corrupts the ordering used by ZSCAN and makes duplicated spans artificially resistant to ZPOPMIN eviction; the merge should use an aggregate such as MAX that preserves a real timestamp.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The redirect-following loop previously allowed depth 10000 and documented that deeper segment trees might not be joined correctly. Reducing it to 1000 without a corresponding product limit means traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 are split into multiple segments, producing incomplete segments and incorrect root/segment assignment. Deep-tree tests only exercise a handful of spans and do not cover this regression.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently truncates segments using a hardcoded limit
findings.body: The script always ZPOPMIN-evicts down to 1000 spans, ignoring SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (whose Python default is 1001 and which callers can configure), and records no metric or log for discarded spans. Legitimate large segments are now silently flushed as incomplete data rather than being handled by the previous explicit oversized-segment path. Because eviction removes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores and the separate has-root flag is not recomputed, an evicted segment/root span can also leave the has-root state inconsistent with the remaining payloads, while evicted span IDs remain in the redirect hash until expiry.

findings.title: Flush-time max_segment_spans protection is removed and the setting becomes dead
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces self.max_segment_spans or emits the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log; after this change the constructor setting has no remaining effect in the flush path. Any segment that bypasses the Lua cap, including data produced by another writer or a future merge change, can now be loaded and emitted without the previous span-count bound, risking oversized Kafka messages and memory pressure. If insert-time eviction is intended to replace this check, the obsolete setting and its contract should be removed consistently rather than left silently ignored.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction or sorted-set merge behavior
findings.body: The updated buffer tests only add the required end_timestamp_precise field to existing small cases; every scenario uses at most five spans. There is no test that inserts more than the eviction limit, verifies which spans are retained, checks behavior when the segment/root span would be evicted, exercises duplicate payloads across merged sorted sets, or verifies redirect chains near the reduced depth limit. The central behavioral change of the PR is therefore untested.
